claim: Every lesson in the catalog comes from a rule that ran in a real project, with its evidence recorded.
note: The checker requires an evidence field on every lesson, but whether that evidence is true is a maintainer's call at review.

claim: A Technical Lead writes a plan with testable acceptance criteria and waits for approval before any code is written.
note: A rule every session loads. Nothing in the self-test runs a model, so following it is not measured.

claim: Every feature gets a separate QA agent that runs your checks and records the evidence.
note: The agent files and the rule that routes to them are checked on every render; whether a session delegates is not.

claim: Retros turn real misses into rules, and prunes delete rules that never fire.
note: The self-test runs the prune counter on fresh and filled installs. The retro itself is written by the model and is not replayed.

claim: The guard blocks protected-branch pushes, force-pushes, secret files, a bare env, remote database writes and any change that would switch it off; asks before deploys, publishes, merges, connector writes, unknown downloads and other edits to its settings; blocks everything if it can't run.
note: Every case replays on the sample projects. It stops accidents, not intent: tests/known-gaps.md lists what it does not see.

claim: Every change to the kit runs a self-test that installs it into sample projects, replays the guard's cases and brings the previous release up to date.
note: The results page is regenerated by scripts/trust-report.sh; a stale page is its own problem and not checked here.

claim: Every feature records an estimated dollar cost from Claude Code's own transcripts, split by agent.
note: The self-test runs the script on a project with no transcripts. Pricing accuracy against a real bill is not checked, which is why the README calls it an estimate.

claim: Branches, environments, checks, modules, risk areas, models, effort and loop limits live in one harness.config.yml; every rule and checklist is a plain Markdown file.
note: Every config key must be documented and every documented key must exist; each module can be added and removed.

claim: New or existing repos, monorepos, folders that aren't a git repo, any language or framework.
note: Closest measurable proxy: the kit renders and checks clean on four sample projects (Go, Python, a monorepo, Next.js). Not covered: other stacks, a repo with its own agent setup, and a folder with no git.

claim: Not a sandbox, doesn't make the model smarter, clear small requests use a lean path.
note: The limits are stated and the lean path is documented; how much it saves in a session is not measured.

claim: Paste one prompt into Claude Code and the agent installs the harness by following INSTALL.md.

proofs.contains: Ask the user before anything that leaves the repo

note: Whether the install is easy is a human judgement. Proxy: the render and its self-checks run on four sample projects. Not covered: the conversation itself.

claim: Adding the marketplace and installing the plugin gives the /morph-* skills.
note: The manifests are checked for the plugin name; the real marketplace install is done by hand at release.

claim: scripts/install.sh copies the kit into a repo and never overwrites.
note: The self-test renders the template itself rather than running install.sh, so the never-overwrite claim is read from the script and not replayed.

claim: Needs bash, git, python3, awk and perl, checked by /morph-doctor; every hand-off ends with a Cost line.
note: The doctor skill names every tool the README lists; its checks are run by the model, not replayed.
